Though you preferred the window seat, the issue with the reservation system at the restaurant seated us in the middle of the hall—which you also found regrettable.
你本想坐在靠窗的位置，但由于店内的预定问题，只好坐在里面的位置，对此你也觉得很遗憾。

<color=#a5ab8e>... Some might see a true romantic in you. A man who brings back to life and color an entire day just from a single word whispered by his ex-lover—as though it happened just yesterday. As though he couldn't forget a single thing done in her company.</color>
<color=#a5ab8e>……如果有谁听到的话，一定会觉得你是个浪漫主义者吧。如此一个仅仅根据我说出的一个关键词，就能将整件事描述得像是昨天才发生一般清楚的男人。</color>

<color=#a5ab8e>But your excellent memory is just the logical, mechanical outcome of childhood mnemonic training you were subjected to.</color>
<color=#a5ab8e>实际上，那出色的记忆力不过是从小经过反复和习惯性的训练积累而成的机械性结果而已。</color>

<color=#a5ab8e>You've got it wrong, though. It wasn't the window seat I was angry about that day.</color>
<color=#a5ab8e>但……不是那样的。我之所以生气，并不是因为没能坐在靠窗的位置。</color>

<color=#a5ab8e>I was angry because the first thing you said when you saw my new dress was that I should return it and get something a size larger.</color>
<color=#a5ab8e>而是你一开始看到我新买的连衣裙，就对我说让我换成大一号的比较好这句话让我心情很糟糕。</color>

It was true that you needed to go up a size. The tightness of the outfit was presenting various difficulties in mundane activities.
那是事实。你实际上确实因为那件衣服而在日常行为动作中感到了不便。
Right, but did you have to say that to my face? You could've just complimented my dress and moved on. 这些话留在心里也可以啊。本来你只需要说一句很棒就行了。

<color=#a5ab8e>Anyway, the initial discomfort slowly receded to the back of my mind the longer I wore that dress.</color>
<color=#a5ab8e>你知道吗？一直穿着那件连衣裙的话，在不知不觉间就会忘记最开始感觉到的那种紧束感了。</color>

<color=#a5ab8e>But when I changed into something more comfortable... That stifling discomfort rushed in all at once, and I realized that, all along, I had been wrestling with an outfit that wasn't made for my size.</color>
<color=#a5ab8e>等到换上另一套舒适的衣服后，才清楚地明白。原来那根本不是适合我的尺码。</color>

<color=#a5ab8e>It's a fitting analogy for that Rouge, too... Though, unlike me, she's refused to change into something more comfortable.</color>
<color=#a5ab8e>那人也是一样。只是如果说与我有什么不同的话，那就是她甚至拒绝换一套衣服。</color>

The voice of whom I presume to be Meursault's mother is still playing from somewhere behind the walls—the voice that will never again speak new words.
墙外仍传来被认为是默尔索的母亲的声音。在许久以前，便已消失的声音。
